name: json_schema
description: Validate JSON documents against a JSON Schema in DuckDB SQL. Check required fields and value types, or fill in defaults defined by your schema.

cta.title: Validate JSON in SQL
cta.description: Install JSON Schema to enforce data contracts on JSON columns at query time — useful for API ingest checks, ETL data-quality gates, and config validation.

quickStart.title: Check two JSON documents
quickStart.description: The schema requires an integer id. The first document passes; the second has a string where an integer is required. All sample data is included.
quickStart.note: Validation raises an error for a nonconforming document. `TRY` turns that error into `NULL`; `COALESCE` makes the result `false`. Validate a schema separately before using this pattern with your own data, because `TRY` also catches errors in the schema. In the DuckDB 2.0 build, `json_schema_is_valid(definition, payload)` returns the boolean directly.

introduction.title: Check that JSON documents follow an agreed structure
paragraphs: A JSON Schema describes a document’s expected fields, types, and constraints. DuckDB can read JSON with different shapes; this extension adds an explicit check against the contract you choose.

Use it to check API payloads or incoming records before further processing. The DuckDB 2.0 build supports JSON Schema drafts 4 through 2020-12 and adds boolean and structured-error functions; the Haybarn 1.5 build targets draft-07. Both can apply schema-defined defaults.

notice.title: DuckDB 2.0 build: full draft support and new functions
notice.body: The DuckDB 2.0 build validates drafts 4, 6, 7, 2019-09 and 2020-12 (2020-12 when `$schema` is absent), asserts `format`, and adds [`json_schema_is_valid`](#json_schema_is_valid) and [`json_schema_errors`](#json_schema_errors). Some documents that the draft-07-only validator accepted are now rejected. See [Changes in the DuckDB 2.0 release](#changes-in-the-duckdb-20-release).
